label:
Litmus milk
(test medium)
note: Same family as Blotto: skim milk powder used as a lab reagent, not eaten. A related skim-milk test medium is skim milk agar.

about.text: Skim milk with the dye litmus, kept in tubes to see what a bacterium does to milk: sours the lactose, clots or digests the casein, or bleaches the dye. It has been a classroom and diagnostic medium for identifying species for a century.

steps.note: Skim milk powder about 100 g/L with litmus at 0.5–5 g/L, some adding 0.5 g/L sodium sulphite.

facts.v: Lactose fermented: pink to red (red below pH 4.5), casein may clot; gas in the clot is a stormy clot
Protein broken down, ammonia or amines: blue (above pH 8.3), sometimes soft blue clot from rennin-like enzyme
Casein digested, clot dissolves, medium clears
Litmus bleached to white under oxygen-free conditions; thioglycollate or an iron nail for anaerobes such as Clostridium
